cards.text: Job's three friends have argued with him round after round, and now they stop answering him, because he was righteous in his own eyes. The room goes so quiet you could hear a sprinkle land. That kindles the anger of somebody new: Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram.

cards.question: Elihu burns with anger against Job. Why?

answers.text: He justified himself rather than God
He spoke before the older men
He ignored all of Elihu's advice

cards.question: Elihu burns with anger against Job's three friends too. Why?

answers.text: They condemned Job without refuting him
They refused to let Elihu say a word
They took Job's side against Elihu

cards.text: Here's the thing. Elihu has been sitting through ALL those speeches, waiting to talk to Job, and I bet his foot fell asleep twice.

cards.question: Why has Elihu waited so long to speak to Job?

answers.text: The others were older than he
Job told him to stay quiet

cards.text: When Elihu sees the three men have no further reply, his anger is kindled, and he finally speaks. He starts by saying he's young in years, and they're old.

cards.question: Elihu says being young made him timid and afraid to tell the older men what he knows.

cards.text: Elihu says he figured age should speak, and many years should teach wisdom. He's the new hire who sits through the WHOLE meeting, waiting for the folks with twenty years at the company to go first.

cards.question: But Elihu says it isn't only years that give a person understanding. What does he say does?
Elihu says wisdom doesn't belong only to the ___.

cards.text: So he says, “Listen to me; I too will declare what I know.” He reminds them he waited while they spoke and listened as they searched for words.

cards.question: Elihu says that after all that talking, one of the three friends finally proved Job wrong.

cards.text: Then he tells the friends not to claim, “We have found wisdom; let God, not man, refute him.” Ooh. Elihu is NOT holding back.

cards.question: Elihu points out that Job hasn't aimed his words at him. So how does Elihu say he'll answer Job?

cards.text: The friends are dismayed and words have escaped them, Elihu says. Friend, I KNOW that feeling, because I went years in a junk drawer without telling a single joke.

cards.question: Now that the friends are silent, Elihu asks if he must keep waiting. Nope, he says he'll answer too. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The friends asked him to speak

cards.question: Elihu paints a picture of what all those words feel like inside him. What is it?

cards.text: He says, “I must speak and find relief; I must open my lips and respond.” That's you in a silent room holding in a sneeze that is NOT staying in.

cards.question: Elihu says he'll be partial to no one. He also promises he won't ___ any man.

cards.text: He says he doesn't even know how to flatter, or his Maker would remove him in an instant. Elihu is just warming up, friend, and this story is far from done.
